metadata.title: AI-ETL: data pipelines that explain themselves

landing.whyTitle: “Why not upload the spreadsheet to a chat and ask?”
landing.whyBody: Fair question. For one file and one question, a chat works. AI-ETL is for where that stops working.

differentiators.title: Many sources in one specification
differentiators.body: CSV, Excel, PDF and DOCX, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB and SQLite databases, and REST APIs. An agent decides how to combine them.

differentiators.title: A pipeline that stays, not an answer that fades
differentiators.body: Every run keeps the generated code, the plan and the quality report. You can review, compare and run it again.

differentiators.title: Infrastructure, not a conversation
differentiators.body: A saved pipeline runs on its own schedule, with approval before writing if you want it.

differentiators.title: Governance from the start
differentiators.body: Data isolated per account in the database, generated code run in isolation with a time limit, and a record of every action.

landing.howBody: The ETL layer is a graph with shared state: each agent receives the state, does one thing and passes it on. The analysis layer works on the data already loaded.
landing.howEtlNote: Only planning and transformation use the model. Extraction, quality and loading are deterministic. If the quality gate blocks, nothing is written and the reason is recorded.
landing.howAnalysisNote: The business question becomes descriptive and predictive sub-analyses. Each one generates code, runs in isolation and is repaired if it fails. The Advisor turns them into prioritised recommendations.
landing.auditBody: The model writes, the system runs and records. You can check every step.

auditCards.title: The code of every step
auditCards.body: Every transformation is a Python function you can read, copy and run again.

auditCards.title: The gate before loading
auditCards.body: Missing values, duplicates, types and outliers are checked before writing. Above the limit, nothing reaches the destination.

auditCards.title: The trail of every action
auditCards.body: Each pipeline agent records what it did and when, next to the code and the quality report.

landing.dualTitle: Made for two people in the same company
landing.dualOperatorTitle: Whoever builds the report by hand today
landing.dualOperatorBody: Configures the source, writes the specification, audits the generated code before trusting it. Reads Python and pandas, but no longer writes it all from scratch every week.
landing.dualExecTitle: Whoever receives the result and configures nothing
landing.dualExecBody: Wants the answer and the recommendation without depending on a number the AI may have made up, because someone on the team could check where it came from.
landing.techTitle: Built for production, not only for a demo
techFacts: Multi-agent orchestration with LangGraph and explicit state
Generated code runs in isolation, with a time limit
Per-account isolation with Row-Level Security in PostgreSQL
Automatic retry and health of scheduled runs
Output checked before it reaches you
Spend cap, cost estimate and approval before loading

faq.q: Does all my data go to the model?
faq.a: No. To write the transformation, the model receives each source's schema and a three-row sample. The generated code runs in isolation, over the whole table.

faq.q: What if the generated code is wrong?
faq.a: If it fails, the code and the error go back to the model, up to three attempts. After that the run ends as a failure with the reason recorded, and everything generated stays saved to read.

faq.q: How do I know the data is good?
faq.a: A deterministic quality gate checks missing values, duplicates, types and outliers before loading. If a column passes 20% missing values, nothing is written to the destination.

faq.q: Which sources and destinations are supported?
faq.a: CSV, Excel, JSON, PDF and DOCX files; PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB and SQLite databases; REST APIs. Destinations: CSV, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB and Parquet on S3.

faq.q: How much does a run cost?
faq.a: You see an estimate before running and can set a monthly cap. In the case study, with the default model, each run cost less than one US cent.

faq.q: Can I schedule runs and require approval?
faq.a: Yes. Pipelines that read databases or APIs run on their schedule, and you can require approval before writing to the destination.

landing.finalCtaTitle: Stop reconciling sources by hand every week
landing.finalCtaBody: Describe what you want. Read the code. Approve the load.

roster.description: Reads the specification and plans the pipeline (sources, transformations, destination).
Extracts and inspects the data from each source (CSV, Postgres, REST, PDF/DOCX).
Generates and runs (in a sandbox) the cleaning and transformation code: the Silver layer.
Checks for nulls, duplicates, and outliers in the transformed data.
Persists the cleaned data to the configured destination.
Breaks the business question down into sub-analyses (Gold and/or Science).
Generates pandas code, computes KPIs, and builds the chart for each descriptive sub-analysis.
Trains a predictive model (scikit-learn) and generates forecasts.
Synthesizes Gold + Science into prioritized, actionable recommendations.
